This is not an admitted Actor state: it falsifies dropping the occupied-query or surviving-key-width premises. Two unit tests pass; the zero-match external harness earns no runtime/caller credit.

The mixed-delta census (`sdk2609-mixed-delta-census/qualification.json`) applies the lookup distinction to the existing code-bound signed-wide source on both presets. Its [observer](../template/runtime/examples/actor_retention_fixture/wide_close.rs) runs after finalization, using retained parent TOP, cloned deltas and isolated proof databases; it adds no live read or source mutation. Each original key records hash/absence-path support separately from complete value availability. Both presets have 108 union keys: 45 originally occupied and 63 absent, including 49 Actor keys (34 occupied, 15 absent). Observed key width is at most 81 bytes; this is not a complete initial-state or configured-domain proof.

| Dirty snapshot | Occupied put | Occupied delete | Absent put | Absent delete |

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| Prefix: 67 keys | 16 | 6 | 36 | 9 |

| Body: 96 keys | 16 | 27 | 35 | 18 |

| Final: 108 keys | 17 | 28 | 31 | 32 |

The final proof supports all 108 original hash/absence paths but cannot return the old 1374-byte System::Events value. Complete mixed-delta replay still succeeds: an original mutation path must not automatically be priced as a full old-value read. The body proof lacks four paths among body-dirty keys (LastAuthoredBlock, BlockWeight, Events, ParentHash); XcmpQueue::OutboundXcmpStatus adds one final-only missing path. SovereignIndex and ActorStateHolds retain complete body lookup yet need their separate repair nodes. These observations do not prove batch additivity or independently necessary whole-call costs.

Thirty union keys have body hash-path support without membership in the recorded-key map. Neither that membership nor an effective overlay value is a complete read trace; missing membership does not prove an overlay-only read occurred. Likewise, 34 final values equal their parent state, including absent deletes, but equality does not exclude earlier or repeated writes or make them free. Three raw-key labels remain outside StorageInfo (extrinsic index, intrablock entropy, transaction level); exact bytes are retained without inventing typed namespace ownership. Original absent paths, batch repair, initial-state validity and independent CPU/backing remain qualification gates.

An exact source inverse removes only the census and its two trie imports, preserving the builder, caller, source geometry and existing guards. Native/SDK checks retain 67/96/108 dirty keys, 122→131 proof nodes, 16987 proof bytes, frozen bills and custody. The new ten sealed exports are separately retained read-only: both PVD files match the earlier issue, while the other eight files differ. They have native/SDK evidence only; earlier secure PVF acceptance and CPU samples remain bound to the earlier tuple. The existing default-library integration regression also passes; no production runtime, weights, Wasm, client pins or worker implementation changed.

The trigger needs a present key that extends an absent removal key, and the typed domain cannot telescope. Typed keys are `Twox128(pallet) || Twox128(item) || suffix`; all240 storage items expose one distinct32-byte prefix, which rules out the cross-item case because two items can never share thirty-two prefix bytes. Within one item an equal-width hashed map has no length difference to exploit, while a concat map embeds `hash(key) || key`, so a shorter key extending a longer one needs a hasher collision. A [regression](../template/runtime/src/tests/integrity_tests.rs) asserts that metadata half over every storage item.

Raw or Root-authored keys stay outside that argument, so they remain the named exposure. No dependency bump repairs the branch: `trie-db`0.32.0 is the newest published version, and upstream `paritytech/trie` master is whitespace-identical to it. A local vendor patch would change the compiled runtime Wasm and rebind every production pin, so it is an owner-visible decision rather than a routine fix. Absent-deletion cost therefore stays unqualified even though the typed path is not a trigger under the stated premises.

The raw exposure is privileged rather than public. A runtime-wide search of the pallet, primitive and runtime sources found only two writers outside the typed domain: the Actors `BenchmarkHelper::prepare_maximum_xcm_version_discovery` fixture, which sets the32-byte `PolkadotXcm::VersionDiscoveryQueue` prefix and clears the32-byte `CurrentMigration` key, and the staking `:deos:benchmark:native-security-mode` fixture key. Both sit behind `#[cfg(feature = "runtime-benchmarks")]`, and the helper trait is gated the same way in [lib.rs](../template/pallets/actors/src/lib.rs), so a production build holds neither key nor write.

Arbitrary raw storage therefore needs a Root call through `System::set_storage`, `kill_storage` or `kill_prefix`, which the existing [origin regression](../template/runtime/src/tests/integrity_tests.rs) admits only for Root. The trigger additionally needs a removal whose key is absent and still a strict prefix of a present key, so the practical exposure is a privileged or upgrade-time liveness fault rather than a public attack path. That classification is why this gate records the vendor-patch decision instead of forcing it.

The three required positive runtime scenarios currently fail with one typed cause rather than three defects. `productive_run_completion_closes_runtime_actor_after_committed_transfer`, `zero_step_and_productive_cleanup_complete_path_matrix_is_exact` and `full_executive_w5_lifecycle_retry_cleanup_fixture_preserves_prefixes` all end in `ModuleError { index: 55, error: [21,0,0,0] }`, which the pallet metadata decodes as the Actors `BehaviorPolicyUnavailable`; index55 is `Actors` in the runtime pallet table. That error is raised where an authored `close_when` requires `close_control_weight_for_contract` to exist and to fit the certificate's maximum lifecycle weight, so all three are gated by the same unqualified policy and resource binding as the owner work. They stay unqualified until that admission exists; rewriting the fixtures onto a no-policy path would be a refusal rewrite and is excluded.

The Actors package suite reports 965 passed, 10 failed and 2 ignored in release, and all ten failures carry that same typed refusal, so they name one policy surface rather than ten defects. One earlier eleventh failure, `stop_cycle_commits_prefix_and_completes_before_unreachable_suffix`, was a stale expectation instead: it asserted a Pipeline Machine fee of 200 in two places, while §8.4 prices the Pipeline envelope through one `WeightToFee` term with wait backing added separately, this mock's `WeightToFee` is the constant 100, and the reachable-StopCycle envelope test already asserts 100 for the same shape. Correcting those two expectations to 100 makes the test pass without touching runtime behaviour, and the suite then reports 965/10/2.

The same rule holds on the real close source (`sdk2609-real-delete-repair/qualification.json`). Rebuilding a fresh memory trie from the prepared218-key TOP reproduces the parent root, and replaying each of the28occupied deletions in isolation shows15 that need no read beyond their own lookup and13 that need exactly one extra node, with none needing more; the largest such node is315bytes, matching the earlier ActorStateHolds completion. The classification is per-deletion and per-instance: it licenses no per-delete tariff, it does not sum into a whole-call price, and surviving-node encoding plus shared path structure remain the explanatory variables. Before this gate the same source recorded only that deletions needed repair in some cases, so the fifteen zero-repair deletions were previously indistinguishable from the thirteen that do read.

Deletion repair reads follow node out-of-lineness rather than key count. One [batch regression](../template/runtime/src/tests/integrity_tests.rs) deletes six occupied keys from a canonical V1 trie, using four single-sibling clusters plus one nested key/descendant pair, and records their lookups first. When every surviving sibling encodes below the32-byte child threshold, the recorded lookup proof replays the whole batch with zero extra reads. When survivors are out of line, the recorded proof alone fails and the complete six-delete batch needs exactly one extra33-byte node. Repair cost is therefore neither per-key additive nor ignorable: it follows the surviving node encoding and path sharing, and this finite observation is not a tariff or a whole-call bound.

The generated-weight drift is now closed. `pallet_tmc`, `pallet_oracle` and `pallet_deos_router` were regenerated with the sanctioned bencher, and the thirty-two `pallet_deos_actors` owners whose doc blocks referenced retired storages were regenerated through focused `--extrinsic` generation spliced into the accepted file. A full Actors bulk run cannot complete: three production benchmarks still abort, namely `process_due_parked_balance_review` at the future-window guard and the two `scheduler_inner_suspended_head_*_complete` fixtures whose actor is no longer in `ServiceNodes`. The audit now reports its passing verdict, down from forty-one stale references.

Two owners are carried rather than re-measured and say so in the trait. `maximum_context_inherent` dispatches the declared maximum inbound context (512 downward messages of64 KiB), which exceeds a legal block's XCMP enqueue weight, and `pipeline_admission_apoptosis` is classified by the script itself as an isolated diagnostic that must not become a coefficient; both keep documented trait defaults preserving their last measured or declared values, and a future successful measurement overrides them. Their remaining record is an open release item, not a silent substitution.

The acceptance gate is now traced to one method pair. `close_control_weight_for_contract` builds its bound from `close_dispatch_weight_upper` plus the authority's `behavior_close_additional_weight` and `financial_wait_close_additional_weight`; [`RuntimeAdmissionCertificateAuthority`](../template/runtime/src/configs/actor_config.rs) implements only `current()`, so both methods fall back to the trait default in [adapters.rs](../template/pallets/actors/src/adapters.rs) that returns `None`. An authored `close_when` therefore refuses at `BehaviorPolicyUnavailable` before any resource is priced, which is exactly what the three runtime scenarios and the ten package policy scenarios report.

The six Close-only price ports are now enumerated: `AdmissionCertificateAuthorityProvider::{behavior_close_additional_weight, financial_wait_entry_weight, financial_wait_close_additional_weight, financial_wait_due_weight, financial_wait_service_weight, financial_wait_ingress_weight}`. All six declare their contract in [adapters.rs](../template/pallets/actors/src/adapters.rs) and default to `None`; the runtime authority implements only `current()`, so no production owner exists for any of them. The pallet mock supplies prepared model coordinates with toggles, which are test witnesses rather than coefficients, and the sanctioned bencher exposes `financial_wait_record_binding` as an extra diagnostic rather than a mergeable owner.

Measuring a whole policy-bearing close is blocked by the same gate. `scheduler.rs:5973` refuses `BehaviorPolicyUnavailable` inside the per-dispatch admission check, so any dispatch of an actor whose contract authors `close_when` or `AwaitFunding` first requires `close_control_weight_for_contract(..).is_some()`. A new production benchmark that staged a live policy-bearing User and called the public Close therefore aborted during setup rather than measuring; it and its trait method were reverted, and both files are byte-identical to their pre-attempt digests. Fragments below the gate remain measurable through the existing diagnostics, but their work is not disjoint, so the supplement cannot be summed from them or obtained by subtracting the plain close.

Either the close resource contract is split into two provably disjoint measured owners, or the per-dispatch gate is narrowed to the paths where an actual Close can occur and policy-bearing execution is admitted meanwhile under a stated bound; both are contract changes that stay with the owner's checkpoint.

Binding those two methods needs certified owners for the optional policy and monitor destruction work, which the package architecture already names as missing (`WeightInfo` has no dedicated Trigger/Deadline removal or complete Parked-release owner) and forbids deriving by subtraction. The six Close-only price ports are that owner set, and the tariff-candidate route is the intended pricing mechanism for them rather than a plain `WeightInfo` coefficient. The three broken benchmarks remain a prerequisite for re-measuring the policy fixtures they cover.

The absent-removal premise is falsified at the selected trie version (`sdk2609-absent-prefix-deletion/qualification.json`). Removing a key absent from the trie is not a general no-op. When the query ends exactly at a value-bearing `NibbledBranch` whose compressed partial continues past the query and that node has one used child, `fix_inner` merges the child after advancing past the end of the query key. Only `debug_assert` guards that advance, so the following `left()` panics with `range end index 18 out of range for slice of length 17`. Absent queries at plain `Branch` nodes already return `Restore`, which shows the intended no-op contract; `TrieBackendEssence::storage_root` forwards `None` entries to `delta_trie_root` unfiltered, so the branch sits on the ordinary state-root path. Cached trie-db0.30,0.31 and0.32 share the unguarded pattern, and no cached version repairs it.

A retained reproduction and its exact panic accompany the gate. One [regression](../template/runtime/src/tests/integrity_tests.rs) keeps the covered subset: an absent deletion whose query diverges inside the branch is a no-op, leaves the root unchanged and replays from its read proof. In the prepared218-key fixture TOP, none of the32absent-final-delete union keys is a strict prefix of a present key and none extends one, on either preset; that is a fixture-scoped necessary-condition negative on real keys, not global unreachability. Absent-deletion cost therefore stays unqualified until the trigger is excluded by the typed key domain or the dependency is repaired.

Fabricated fixture exports are not byte-reproducible, and the cause is signature randomization rather than proof ordering. Three runs of the unchanged export produced eight differing files while all24printed runtime invariants stayed identical, including the post root, the67/96/108dirty keys, the122→131node union and the16987proof bytes; only the PVD file matched. The differing regions are the64-byte signature inside the signed extrinsic, the64-byte Aura seal in the header digest, and the header extrinsics root that a changed signature implies. `sp_core::sr25519::Pair::sign` forwards to schnorrkel, [which documents a randomized nonce](https://github.com/paritytech/schnorrkel/blob/main/src/sign.rs), so one key signs the same message differently on every run; the fixture signs both the extrinsic and the seal with sr25519.

Proof ordering is not a factor: [`StorageProof`](https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk/blob/7a8daa68e18718c18823c1109513fdc1c8aa71fe/substrate/primitives/trie/src/storage_proof.rs) stores `trie_nodes: BTreeSet<Vec<u8>>`, so `new`, `merge` and every recorder drain collapse into one canonical deduplicated order. Retained artifact sets therefore stay valid for their own instance while a downstream pin must bind a retained instance rather than a fresh run; deterministic signing would be the only way to make these files regenerable and no supported sr25519 path offers it. A [characterization test](../template/runtime/tests/signed_wide_close.rs) pins the randomization so a future derandomization forces requalification instead of silently changing evidence identity.

The deferred-write CPU route gate (`sdk2609-deferred-write-cpu-route/qualification.json`) distinguishes pallet measurement from database calibration. The existing benchmark body timer/proof snapshot precedes commit_db. Its Ext commit drains storage changes, materializing the root when needed, then BenchmarkingState applies the trie transaction and reopens the database; logical write tracking names changed storage keys, not physical trie-node writes. The later storage_root_time cannot recover that intervening work. [Configured RocksDbWeight](../template/runtime/src/weights/rocksdb_weights.rs) remains 25,000/100,000 ns per read/write with zero ProofSize; its broad sanity test is not calibration evidence.

| SDK storage write mode | Timed owner | Applicability limit |

| --- | --- | --- |

| ImportBlock | Replacement delta, trie root, insertion-only transaction conversion and database commit, divided by batch size | Removals/pruning excluded; cleanup commit occurs after timing |

| ValidateBlock | Separate storage-test Wasm calls with in-memory proof-backed root, minus dry-run and averaged per key/round | No persistent DB commit; not the DEOS runtime or a complete PVF test |

The locked [storage runner](https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk/blob/7a8daa68e18718c18823c1109513fdc1c8aa71fe/substrate/utils/frame/benchmarking-cli/src/storage/write.rs) selects existing snapshot entries and replaces each with random bytes of the same length. Both paths supply Some(value), never a delete. ValidateBlock records old lookup proofs before calling its dedicated storage-access Wasm; that payload cannot express None. The import timer deliberately skips trie removals/pruning. Snapshot geometry, batch size, seed, cache/recorder mode, input/output bytes and timing scope therefore belong to the calibration contract. Default batch averaging or same-value-length overwrites do not establish deletion-sibling/root/commit cost for Close, and their fees cannot be inferred from the current constants.

The exact selected frame-omni-bencher binary advertises storage in inherited help but rejects its execution: only pallet and overhead are dispatched. The gate observes exit 1 and no creation of the supplied isolated database path; no collection ran. Immutable [command source](https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk/blob/7a8daa68e18718c18823c1109513fdc1c8aa71fe/substrate/utils/frame/omni-bencher/src/command.rs) agrees with that boundary. [benchmarks.sh](../scripts/benchmarks.sh) exposes pallet collection only, so adding a wrapper flag cannot supply the missing backend. Five complete SDK storage-calibration sources are associated in the gate; this does not attest an auxiliary Wasm or execute native import/PVF calibration.

A deletion-aware deferred owner must identify validation versus native persistence, source-preserving initial state and complete mixed delta, recorder/cache/batch conditions, rollback and exact timing endpoints before collection. Reuse the existing signed/native root witnesses as semantic sources, not CPU samples; they do not implement BenchmarkingState's commit controls. The full proof-backed validate_block route below is now operational; isolated mutation/root CPU and native persistence still need their own owners, without a parallel observer/database stack or runtime hooks. Production binding still requires complete non-overlapping owners and backing; neither generic SDK calibration nor an unavailable command authorizes a coefficient.

Runtime StorageInfo supplies the storage namespace labels, not economic cost ownership. The earlier empty-code eight-node finalization union includes shared and non-Actor work and cannot become an eight-node Actors tariff. Conversely, newly dirty signed Actor deletions prevent treating every deferred witness as automatically fixed system overhead. UserDispatch and FRAME counters, final telemetry, custody/hold release and SDK builder/import/refusal checks remain unchanged. Complete mutation-bound RefTime/ProofSize, root/commit price, arbitrary namespaces/callers and independent backing remain unqualified; no metric transfers to the separate carry proofs.

Ordinary TestExternalities does not implement the SDK benchmark backend's commit/tracking controls. It cannot impersonate BenchmarkingState to force `run_benchmark` through that lifecycle. The native consumer uses ordinary commit/root/recorder APIs directly and needs no database delegation or observer stack. The prior reference-route audit retains the complete immutable CLI/default-backend source evidence; its interface gap is closed by the native bridge, not by changing SDK visibility or benchmark lifecycle.

The joined `close_dormant_event_root` diagnostic places reset and prefix production after timer start, then includes roots before and after public Dormant Close. It therefore measures materialization and root work with current-block Append authority, including compact-count widening from 63, while retaining prefix production as a measured owner. The root-caller gate (`sdk2609-root-caller-domain/qualification.json`) rejects transferring that diagnostic to the canonical Parked signed-wide source: changing only the timer does not change its Dormant state, measured 63-remark prefix or raw-origin caller into the required source. Adding a root to another pallet benchmark would still select that backend, not automatically the parachain validation algorithm. No new selector, Wasm issue or timing campaign follows from this rejection.

| Existing route | Storage/root execution owner | What it cannot establish |

| --- | --- | --- |

| Root-inclusive pallet benchmark | Runtime benchmark plus native host BenchmarkingState/trie backend | Parked signed source, persistent commit interval or PVF root CPU |

The [locked Cumulus implementation](https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk/blob/7a8daa68e18718c18823c1109513fdc1c8aa71fe/cumulus/pallets/parachain-system/src/validate_block/implementation.rs) installs replacement storage functions, including host_root, before executing the verified block against its proof-backed backend. By contrast, [native_api.rs](../template/runtime/examples/actor_retention_fixture/native_api.rs) calls Core/BlockBuilder through the external StateMachine even when RuntimeExecution selects Wasm. Thus a Wasm runtime API label alone is not PVF root-CPU evidence. Complete immutable Cumulus/sp-io source matches support this distinction; no new PVF execution is claimed.

The existing [PVF exporter](../template/runtime/examples/actor_retention_fixture/pvf.rs) can retain the selected signed-wide source, verify its Aura seal and complete native TOP/root, then export code-bound parent/PVD/block/proof and expected output. The [PVF tool](../template/tools/pvf-validation/README.md) is deliberately an acceptance owner: it checks complete results and typed negative outcomes through real workers, without exporting a CPU measurement. Its timeout is a failure boundary, not a tariff or whole-domain maximum; timing the caller's await would mix queue/preparation and execution. Current production-code identity and input agreement still need refresh before new exact-artifact acceptance.

The worker timing gate (`sdk2609-pvf-worker-timing/qualification.json`) binds the existing SDK timing/result path without executing a new candidate. WorkerResponse carries duration, but the public ValidationHost oneshot returns only ValidationResult or ValidationError. The queue retains successful duration for its `parachain::pvf` trace event, then sends the result without that field. The [tool](../template/tools/pvf-validation/src/main.rs) retains Metrics::default() and no capture by default. Its optional host-only capture is described below; a public result, source-visible field or existing trace site alone is not proof that telemetry was collected.

| Timing surface | Actual quantity | Scope limitation |

| --- | --- | --- |

| WorkerResponse.duration | Difference of RUSAGE_CHILDREN user+system CPU, represented in microseconds | Whole completed job child, not isolated Wasm call or root |

| polkadot_pvf_execution_time | Host HistogramTimer around assigned worker start_work | Wall time, including communication/setup/cleanup; not child CPU |

| Execution queued time | Queue waiting elapsed before worker assignment | Separate scheduling delay |

| Tool submit/await timer, if added | Caller wall time across the host pipeline | May include queue/preparation; currently not a measurement |

The immutable [execute-worker source](https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk/blob/7a8daa68e18718c18823c1109513fdc1c8aa71fe/polkadot/node/core/pvf/execute-worker/src/lib.rs) takes cumulative child usage before launching its sequential job and after waitpid. The common helper sums user and system time. Artifact file read/checksum, PoV decompression and input encoding occur in the parent worker; even work after the first counter read is not child CPU. The child includes process/thread setup and monitoring, runtime construction/instantiation, validate_block, result decoding and response work. Thus duration excludes host queues and compilation but is broader than PVF call/root execution; changing security/process/thread configuration changes its evidence domain.

The [host worker interface](https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk/blob/7a8daa68e18718c18823c1109513fdc1c8aa71fe/polkadot/node/core/pvf/src/execute/worker_interface.rs) checks the returned CPU duration against the execution timeout, while a separate generous communication timeout uses wall time. The queue traces duration only on its successful-result branch; error branches omit it, and early corrupted-artifact/decompression responses use zero placeholders. These are not valid zero-cost samples. Existing complete-output and typed-negative acceptance must remain authoritative; success trace alone cannot certify the expected ValidationResult.

The [CPU capture](../template/tools/pvf-validation/src/cpu_trace.rs) is opt-in through `pvf-assurance.sh --cpu-trace FILE`; it adds no worker IPC patch, private SDK access or runtime observer. A host-local subscriber matches the execute-queue target/module and exact assignment/success messages. The single outstanding case binds the expected ArtifactId Debug shape from public code/preparation hashes and the assigned worker. Positive acceptance requires exactly one valid duration after complete output equality; negatives retain null CPU. Missing/duplicate/mismatched events, subscriber or output failures, zero/unsupported/fractional-microsecond/overflow durations refuse without a histogram/wall fallback.

Zero-Step has no Task, Action fee, tail or Run. Its semantic-publication source is an intra-attempt carrier, not a separately committed on-chain prefix: outer rollback restores readiness and Pipeline payment. Cadenced control may already have rearmed its independent Trigger pointer before semantic publication. For unpaused unlatched Idle, the planner chooses Protocol Disabled without a window or the independent window-expiry Block deadline; it does not advance a retained Service head. Policy-bearing zero-Step cannot author Parked Balance.

Idle semantic publication does not promote Pending to Live. Terminal retirement deletes the process instead of publishing Disabled and is a different branch.

## Admission Certificate Authority

`configs/actor_config.rs::RuntimeAdmissionCertificateAuthority::current` derives authority from compiled configuration and generated Weight functions, not Actor population or block state. It rebuilds the Control and effect identities, hashes 22 configured-bound fields, including the independent Parked watch bound and both configured `close_when` limits, takes the componentwise maximum of 12 lifecycle bindings and hashes the combined production identity. Those are four hash operations; constructing Weight values does not execute or charge the represented Tasks. This work belongs to the caller's CPU cost, even though it performs no pallet storage access.

`actors_integration_tests::task_effect_weight_provider_owns_all_task_families` runs without externalities and now checks both effect and maximum Control providers for every retained Task family across all legal nonempty Step counts/cursors and Predicate counts. It also covers absent/present predicates on StopCycle. Every retained Task has a fixed field shape; there is no recipient-fanout dimension. An introduced runtime storage, pool, staking or observation read fails this boundary. `admission_authority_is_storage_independent_and_covers_lifecycle_bindings` separately guards authority/identity construction. `admission_authority_binds_behavior_limits_to_certificate_identity` varies either limit independently, preserving semantic/body/Weight identity while changing admission identity without storage mutation. Pure provider calls incur CPU work without ledger/trie proofs. These checks certify neither physical bounds nor economic execution.

The configured-bound digest still includes `ActorMaxFundingTrackedAssets=40`, although generic Actors no longer uses that limit for admission/execution or retains Opening capture/asset-tracking state. Its constant hashing/metadata footprint remains part of this authority, not a forty-asset creation or execution ceiling. The package architecture owns the production absence and public-admission counterexample. Removing this obsolete field requires coordinated Config, authority digest, diagnostic/test and metadata/client ABI changes; this obsolete input remains included while its removal stays a separate coordinated change.

Let `C = ceil(max(ActorMaxContractSteps - 1, 0)/4)`, `P = ActorMaxPredicatesPerStep`, with current reference `C=3` and `P=4`. The following is a source-level evaluation inventory, not generated execution Weight or an allocation/timing measurement.

| Identity input family | Generated Weight evaluations |

| --- | --- |

| User Opening and body reconstruction vectors | `2(C+1)` |

| Opening failure/retry/completion endpoint pairs | `6(C+1)` |

| Opening progress endpoint pairs | `2C` |

| Tail planning | `4` |

| Running and Suspended tail variants | `18(P+1)` |

| Suspended head endpoint pairs | `12` |

| Predicate vectors | `2P + max(P-1, 0)` |

| Fixed Control entries | `13` |

| Effect identity | `10` fixed generated entries; StopCycle contributes zero |

| Lifecycle maximum | `12` entries |

At these bounds, Control identity evaluates 168 generated entries, effect identity 10, and lifecycle maximum 12. The implementation constructs 13 Control vectors and one effect vector; compiler optimization may alter physical allocation/work, so this does not establish RefTime. `RuntimeStepControlWeight::production_weight_identity_from_user_opening`, `TmctolTaskEffectWeight::production_weight_identity` and `RuntimeAdmissionCertificateAuthority::current` own this composition. No cache or per-block memoization is implied.

`admission_authority_is_storage_independent_and_covers_lifecycle_bindings` calls the provider without externalities, checks Control/effect composition, verifies lifecycle dominance with both maximum components attained, and checks unchanged storage roots and equal authority at different block numbers. This proves the current declared composition, not the soundness of its generated coefficients. Known Close underbounds remain; lifecycle compact-Weight width must be refreshed when production bindings change. The package Close inventory and `close_host_authority_calls_belong_to_detachment` attribute one invocation to detachment on successful public Active Close, not one per body reload; Contract commitment hashing remains separate.

The raw-only `admission_certificate_authority` benchmark invokes this provider once inside measurement, including all four hashes and generated-Weight identity construction. A fresh reference benchmark-Wasm run with six timing samples and one database sample reports zero reads, writes and proof bytes. This agrees with the native storage-independent guard; it is scoped CPU evidence for the compiled provider, without qualification of the referenced coefficients, caller composition or production Wasm. The [script entrypoint](../scripts/README.md) owns reproduction and output restrictions; any configuration or binding change requires refreshed construction evidence.

## Control Plane and Read Surfaces

Canonical active projection joins `ActorSemanticStates`, certified Contract fragments, admission identity, `ActorProcesses`, exact Service/Deadline/Parked residence, and optional Run state at one finalized block. Dormant identity, detector topology, dirty-source progress, and bounded simulation remain canonical-chain truth.

The runtime simulation API executes the same package evaluator and finalizer used by scheduler service. Its bounded records carry canonical `StepOutcome` values, including concrete failure cause plus retry disposition, and its status is the shared `AttemptDisposition`; DEOS adds no adapter-side simulation model.

Version 6 `ActorEligibilityApi` reports `NotRegistered`, `Dormant`, or canonical Active classification at one finalized block. It preserves terminal reason, retry/block/timestamp-tick payloads, the four-family Trigger activation shape, latch, and process residence. Clients do not reimplement eligibility. The projection never promises service because Service order and available Weight decide admission.

`ActorCostApi` binds the DEOS `Balance` and returns one bounded canonical quote. User Creation Fee, current family-specific Trigger Weight/fee, upfront Pipeline Machine amount, current maximum Action-effect Weight/fee, and geometry-bound state hold remain separately named. Trigger provenance hashes the six generated occurrence owners; Pipeline provenance carries the admitted runtime/Weight identities; state-hold provenance exposes DEOS pricing of one ED per present component plus one `MICRO_UNIT` per retained SCALE byte. System Actors report zero Actors fees and explicit hold exemption without resource privilege.

`automation/cost.ts` projects `ActorCostApi` without recombining owners and maps committed `ActionFeeCharged` receipts by exact Actor/Cycle/Step coordinates; `adapters/blockchain/actor-cost.ts` invokes the typed API at one caller-supplied finalized hash and returns explicit unavailability instead of local fee inference. `automation/cost-vectors.ts` fail-closes malformed identities, totals, strategies, family/geometry coverage, System exemption, and dormant semantics before generated runtime vectors enter browser validation.

The browser Trigger editor offers exactly Manual, AddressEvent, AtTime, and Cadenced, routes observation comparisons to execution-time Step preconditions, and explains latched-fire coalescing plus Service backpressure. It exposes no Trigger-family bond quote because dispatch owns no such economic surface. The browser's authoring, artifact, matching-Wasm, simulation, observation, and governance-composition surfaces live under `web-client/src/lib/automation/` and `web-client/src/lib/observation/`. They bind metadata and runtime identity rather than recreating pallet semantics.

Unbounded history, archive search, forecasting records, governance preparation history, and longitudinal telemetry remain materialized-provider work under [`actors-control-plane.contract.en.md`](./actors-control-plane.contract.en.md) and [`read-model.contract.en.md`](./read-model.contract.en.md).

Actors try-state reconciles semantic partitions, process status and residence, Service-ring links/count/cursor, Block/Tick Deadline heaps, C32 bucket/vacancy links, generation-bound handles, Park/Pending ownership, owner slots, System sovereign locators, and parked-balance dependency sources/cursors. Retained pre-fork scheduler declarations are rejected as active authority.

The reference Router binds `RuntimeLpPairIntegrity`, so try-state also requires every bounded LP reverse entry to resolve to the exact Asset Conversion pool and LP token, requires that LP asset to exist, and requires complete pool/index cardinality equality. Missing indexes, wrong LP identities, orphan pairs, and deleted LP assets fail before Actors liquidity or Treasury unwind can consume the binding.

| Actors late-failure surface | Injected checkpoint | Restoration evidence |

| --- | --- | --- |

| Transfer / SplitTransfer | Certified placement rejection; second-leg adapter failure | Exact runtime root for direct transfer; all leg balances and no success event for split |

| Mint | Native issuance overflow after read-only preflight | Exact runtime root, including ledger, events, and Actors state |

| SwapIn / SwapOut | Adapter failure after input debit | Actor and pool custody restored; no swap event; only ordinary failed-step accounting may commit |

| Add / Remove Liquidity | First asset debit/credit fault; post-call minimum-output rejection | Package custody rollback plus exact runtime root across ledgers, pool, LP index, issuance, and events |

| Stake / Unstake | Adapter failure after asset/share burn | Custody and staking representations restored; no success event |

| Donate Liquidity | Failure after first asset burn | Both custody legs and donation accounting restored; no success event |

| FeeCollector | Ledger failure after admission | Exact runtime root; no fee receipt, sink movement, attempt mutation, or scheduler drift |

Each task executes inside one task-owned storage transaction. A rejected task restores its adapter writes and task success event; the surrounding attempt may still commit its specified `StepFailed`, counters, policy transition, and later independent steps. Tests distinguish that expected failure envelope from leaked partial adapter state.

`scripts/actors-assurance.sh` owns package portability, external embedding, runtime integration, scheduler fairness, dense/sparse liveness, 10,000-Actor Service stress, and occupancy proof commands. Stress evidence covers cyclic Service fairness and exact Deadline draining. These are configured service-unit measurements, not user-facing time promises.

Recording excludes authoring and diagnostic state enumeration. Shared nodes count once, so removing an absence read need not save proof bytes. This is whole-block native trie evidence, not per-Step marginal cost, full parachain PoV, a production-Wasm certificate or permission to discount generated Weight.

## Rollback and Operational Evidence

Task rollback and lifecycle rollback remain distinct corpus boundaries. A DEX adapter that fails after input transfer restores actor/pool task writes while `ContinueNextStep` permits the following transfer and cycle summary to commit.

Operational-recovery fixtures bind exact runtime version identity, breaker deferral/recovery, Continuation Deadline return, and bounded repair. Version drift yields `EvidenceMismatch` without changing factual Actor state. Breaker activation produces no partial cycle/close evidence; recovery admits the deferred close. A suspended retry wakes at cooldown without another signal, while one-actor permissionless repair remains available under the breaker and performs no hidden task work.

Full-corpus validation requires exclusive Service/Deadline/Parked residence, atomic pre-state restoration, and bounded Weight ownership. Quick Actors acceptance validates this contract; full acceptance executes the anchored runtime corpus.

Operational observation uses the canonical Service head/count/cursor, active limit, Block/Tick Deadline frontiers, actor-local process residence, starvation events, and sweep events. Weight and scan deferral remains silent and state-preserving. These surfaces expose pressure without promising an exact future execution block.

### Capacity Economics

The reference runtime binds `MaxActiveActors = MaxActorIdentities = MaxQueueLength = 10,000`, `MaxOwnerSlots = 255`, `MaxSweepBatch = 5`, and `ActorCreationFee = 2 * EXISTENTIAL_DEPOSIT = 0.002` fee-native units. An all-User 10,000-identity population pays 20 units in nonrefundable creation fees. Both named presets already contain 15 System identities, so filling their remaining 9,985 slots pays 19.97 units and needs at least 40 User owners. Active liveness may additionally require protected balances, which remain actor custody. These configured cost floors exclude ordinary transaction fees and refundable holds and do not certify the creation-backed lifetime-cleanup tariff.

The same 10,000 ceiling bounds simultaneous active Actors and Service residence. One maximum permissionless sweep call examines five explicit identities, so 2,000 full batches cover the complete identity cap. A hypothetical one-batch-per-block sequence spans 12,000 seconds, or 3 hours 20 minutes, at the six-second target; this is a latency illustration, not guaranteed throughput, because dispatch Weight, competing block demand, eligibility, and submitted transaction count control realized progress.

The guaranteed saturated model assumes only one maximum attempt or cleanup fits the reserved Service envelope. With 10,000 eligible residents, no bypass, and one maximum attempt per block, a tail Actor is encountered within one 10,000-block ring traversal. Lighter plans may admit more work, but `MaxExecutionsPerBlock = 1,000` is only a count ceiling. Cadence denotes temporal eligibility; cyclic position and available Weight determine realized service.

Governance can lower the active-admission limit, operate the breaker, and repair bounded scheduler state, but it cannot confiscate or forcibly close a healthy owner-controlled User actor merely to recover capacity. Permissionless sweep closes only actors meeting the specified liveness/expiry conditions. Consequently, a fully funded live identity-cap fill has no bounded governance-only eviction latency in the current contract. DEOS provides explicit finite cost and bounded repair, not adaptive creation pricing or a guarantee against economically funded saturation.

The zombie-spam regression compares the configured actor-cap creation charge plus declared create Weight fees against declared batch-sweep Weight fees. It checks coded fee composition and its 100:1 floor; stale or underbounded generated owners prevent interpreting that ratio as complete physical-cost dominance. Changes to creation fee, fee conversion or sweep bounds require refreshing the applicable fee and physical evidence.
